features.name: Crewed field-gun and howitzer batteries (Yuri cannon system)
features.summary: Artillery-officer troops in a party turn into a fully animated gun battery when they spawn in battle: the officer brings three gunners and a multi-part gun (body, wheels, barrel, ropes, ramrods, shell). The crew walks to stations, swabs, loads, aims, fires; shells fly in an arc and explode with radial damage, craters and morale shock. Field guns fire flat at the officer's AI target; howitzers fire at 45 degrees.
features.mechanics: Spawn: every mission template's ti_on_agent_spawn trigger (e.g. mst:lead_charge/t98) calls cf_YuriSpawnCannon(agent). If the agent is a cannoneer-officer troop (trp_factionplayer_fieldgun_cannoneer_officer..trp_factionplayer_fieldgun_cannoneer) and the team's battery counter team slot 178 (+ allied team's) is below 5 (10 with technology faction slot 416), it spawns 3 crew agents from the faction's crew troop (faction slot 403/404), spawns rope/ramrod/cannonball props, wheels and barrel, then the body last; the body's own ti_on_scene_prop_init (spr_*_body/t0 -> cannon_body_spawn) copies the just-set globals $g_cannoneer_officer/$g_cannoneer1-3/$g_rope1.../$g_barrel into scene_prop slots 192-206 and sets per-model geometry/reload slots 189-191, 209, 210, 213 (0=gun,1=howitzer), 214. Excess officers fade out. Gun model tier (1/2/3) is chosen by technology slots 415/416. Loop: mst:lead_charge/t95 (every 0.033 s) iterates every spr_fieldgun_1_body..spr_fieldgun_1_wheels instance and runs cannon_reassign_cannoneers, cannon_tick_timer, cannon_process_moving, cannon_process_reloading, cannon_process_aiming; scene_prop slot 197 is the state machine (2 arrive ->3 load ->4 aim ->5..7 ready -> 8 fired), slot 196 the countdown timer. cannon_fire plays crew Yuri_* animations, sets the shell prop's flight slots (167 in-flight, 177 projectile type from get_cannoneer_officer_faction_cannon_projectile_type, 178 calibre), animates the shell with prop_instance_animate_to_position (time = distance/150) at a randomised point near agent_ai_get_look_target (howitzer: rotate 45 deg, store target in slots 220-223), bursts psys_cannon_smoke/psys_musket_flash, plays near/far sounds. mst:lead_charge/t96 (every 0.01 s) detects arrival -> shell_hits_pos: 65-95% chance explode_at_pos (radial agent_deliver_damage_to_agent scaled by distance, /10 in trench, /2 prone, knock-down animation, adds suppression to team slot 52+division) else a bounce/crater prop (max 400 craters); gas shells spawn spr_gas_shell. YuriBatteryHoldPosition answers player orders (t97), cf_YuriCannonCanoneersRetreat (t59) handles crew rout.

features.name: Company discipline, suppression and rout
features.summary: Every company (division) in battle has a live discipline score. Taking fire, artillery near-misses and casualties drain it; strength ratio, the faction's army morale, and the player's Captain skill (when the player is near the company) shore it up. Low discipline makes soldiers less accurate and slower, makes them break formation to crouch, and below a threshold the whole company sounds the retreat bugle and runs, rallying once a timer expires.
features.mechanics: Per team (0-3) x division (0-7) team-slot arrays. Writers of penalties: mst:lead_charge/t104 (ti_on_agent_killed_or_wounded) adds 6000/quality(34+div) x formation multiplier to casualty slot 187+div; add_penaltytodiscipline_fromfire_to_target_of_agent (from mg_decide_fire) and explode_at_pos add distance-scaled suppression to slot 52+div; get_company_foramtion_discipline_penalty_multiplier scales by formation type (205+div: 40/90/100/110/120 %); technology 420 reduces penalties 20-25 %. mst:lead_charge/t84 (every 0.2 s) decays suppression by 25 and recomputes discipline 197+div = 9000 - suppression(52) - slot 60 - casualties(187) + 1000 x alive/initial(68/34) - (100 - faction slot 834)/5, -1500 if the player has fallen, + Captain skill (skl_reserved_1, id 3) x 100 if the player is within 20+3xskill m of the company's order point (team 100+div / 108+div); clamp 100..10000. mst:lead_charge/t82 (0.5 s) turns discipline (and fatigue 18+div, stance, gas masks, skirmish mode 263+div, tech 408) into agent_set_accuracy_modifier/speed/damage and stores company accuracy in 179+div. mst:lead_charge/t85 (1 s): at <=80 % discipline soldiers randomly take scripted cover and crouch for 6 s. mst:lead_charge/t86 (1 s): discipline < 1500 + Inspirer skill (id 5) x 100 -> company_retreat + snd_bugle_retreat + message; t87 counts down retreat timer 84+div and calls company_stop_retreat + snd_bugle_stop_retreat. Native decide_run_away_or_not is emptied (0/50 stmts) so this replaces Native's per-agent courage rout.

features.name: Firearm range falloff, headshots and cover in one hit trigger
features.summary: Every rifle/carbine/LMG hit is recomputed: full damage up to 50 m, sliding down to 75 % at 175 m and beyond, doubled on a head hit, scaled by the player's friendly-fire and damage-to-player difficulty options, and cut to a third for siege defenders shot from 10 m or more (they are behind walls).
features.mechanics: mst:lead_charge/t101 (ti_on_agent_hit, present in all 25 templates). Reads the attacking item from reg0; if it is itm_damage_pure, passes damage through. For listed firearm ranges (is_between blocks of rifle families + explicit items) it takes item_get_thrust_damage as base, gets distance in metres between attacker and victim: 50-175 m -> base x (100 - (d-50)/5) %; >=175 m -> 75 %. store_trigger_param 4 (hit bone) == 9 (head) -> x2. If the victim (trigger param 1) belongs to p_main_party and is not the player, options_get_damage_to_friends 0/1 -> /2 or x3/4; if the victim is the player, options_get_damage_to_player 0/1 -> /4 or /2. Siege ($g_battle_type 2) defender hit by non-player at >=10 m -> /3. set_trigger_result.
evidence: dis be mst:lead_charge/t101:conseq lines 91-145: falloff, bone 9 x2, difficulty options, siege /3
all operations vanilla (no WSE)

features.name: Infamy, casus belli and alliance call-to-arms diplomacy
features.summary: Each nation has Infamy (0-150, 'badboy'): declaring war without a claim, breaking alliances or going bankrupt raises it; it decays by 1 every 3 days. Allies are asked to join wars; an ally that refuses breaks the alliance and gains infamy; the player gets a menu to accept or decline. High infamy triggers a world-weariness notification.

features.name: National manpower pool, conscription policy and population-scaled lord count
features.summary: Each nation has a manpower pool that refills from its population according to its conscription policy (volunteer 3 %, limited 10 %, extended 20 %, wide 25 %). Lords and garrisons refill only by drawing from that pool, so long wars exhaust a country. The number of lords a nation fields and their party size scale with population and army-size policy; lords are drawn from (or returned to) a shared pool of lord troops as nations grow, shrink or are annexed.
features.mechanics: faction slots: 769 population, 876 manpower, 877 manpower cap, 878 policy, 879 reinforcement chance %, 825 army-size %, 828 military spending counter. pas_faction_set_conscription_policy(f, 1..4): cap = population/11000 (min 50) x 30/100/200/250 %, re-bases pool, chance = pool x100/800 clamped 5..100. pas_faction_calculate_manpower (per PPS iteration): pool += sqrt(population)/2500 (12..500) x policy factor, clamp -2000..cap. cf_pas_faction_reinforcement_required(f, cost): roll chance (slot 879) then subtract cost from pool. pas_reinforce_party(party): if below party_get_ideal_size and the roll passes (cost 3 for centres, 7 for lords) adds 3+3+1 (or 2+3+1+1 for lords) of the faction's four troop types (faction 809-812), adds 20 to 828, trims excess; adds artillery officers if tech 424 and few guns. pas_get_faction_ideal_lord_number = population/2,000,000 x 825/100 + 3 (3..50). party_get_ideal_size (modified Native) = $preferred_ai_party_size (+25 for the faction leader) or for lords preferred-30 + 4 x ideal lords, clamp 50..200. pas_faction_manage_lord_number (per iteration, max 2 changes): too few -> pas_init_lord takes a factionless lord from trp_knight_1_1..trp_kingdom_1_pretender; too many -> remove_lord_from_game. strig:50 (24 h) respawns defeated lords only if cf_pas_faction_reinforcement_required(f, 0) succeeds. prsnt_pas_menu shows army size, policy slider and penalties to satisfaction/workers.

features.name: PAS lord and marshal AI (direct campaign control)
features.summary: Replaces Native's lord decision-making with a simpler, direct controller: the marshal starts a campaign when at war, half of the lords follow him, the marshal patrols a threatened home centre or a random border centre of the enemy, attacks targets chosen by faction-level scripts, and ends the campaign when the target is invalid or peace is made. Lords not on campaign patrol near home and keep themselves topped up from manpower.
features.mechanics: strig:130 (0.001 h) calls pas_ai_lord_decide for two lords per tick (cursor $async_simple_trigger35 over trp_npc1..trp_knight_1_1_wife). pas_ai_lord_decide (322 stmts): detaches lords sitting in foreign centres, pas_reinforce_party x2 (x5 for marshal), records nearest own centre (party 600); marshal: if at war and pas_faction_get_center_to_defend finds a threatened centre -> 50 % start campaign + patrol it; else start campaign 80 %; campaign states in party slot 581 (0 idle, 3 following marshal, 5/6/7/8 marshal modes) with target party 582 and cooldown 583; faction slot 815 = campaign active. pas_faction_start_campaign: marshal state 8, each idle lord 50 % -> pas_lord_follow_marshall; marshal patrols pas_get_random_war_border_center_for_faction_universal. pas_lord_patrol_center sets party_set_ai_behavior 3 (patrol) with aggressiveness/courage 15, initiative 100, helpfulness 200. pas_faction_end_campaign resets everyone to hold (behavior 2) at current position. Native process_kingdom_parties_ai is gone (async stub empty); npc_decision_checklist_party_ai is still present (99 % Native).
evidence: dis be strig:130, pas_ai_lord_decide (first 150 stmts), pas_faction_start_campaign, pas_faction_end_campaign, pas_lord_patrol_center

features.name: Enlistment office and rank promotion service
features.summary: In a town's enlistment office the player can enlist as a soldier or officer of that nation; the player then rides with an assigned lord, fights his battles, wears the issued uniform and rifle, earns service points over time, and is promoted through ranks - NCO at rank 2, independent high-command officer with 40 men at rank 5, and finally marshal at rank 9.

features.name: National military technology tree with dated inventions
features.summary: Each nation researches about 19 military technologies (rifled muskets, breech-loaders, smokeless powder, modern artillery, skirmish-line and modern attack tactics, machine guns, gas...). Each has an historical year; once that year is reached a nation may invent it at random (faster at higher game speed or for rich nations), and the player can fund research from the budget. Technologies switch what the battle systems allow: gun models, formations, abilities, rifle issued to troops, uniforms.
features.mechanics: faction slots 406-424 hold state (10000 = invented); 425-443 the year each becomes available (slot+19); 768 national budget. strig:113 (24 h): for each live kingdom and tech not invented with year <= $g_current_year, chance 1000/$g_game_speed (halved if budget <= 1000) out of 3000 -> invented, message 'The {s1} has finished researching technology {s2}'. prsnt_faction_technologies shows the tree (pts_create_tech_button, pts_create_selected_tech_name/description, cf_pts_check_tech_availability) with a Research button ('Country does not have enough budget to start research'). Gate predicates cf_if_party_/team_/agent_faction_invented_technology are called from ~250 sites (formation changes: '{s1} cannot change formation - you need to research Skirmish Line Tactics'). strig:123 swaps uniforms when uniform techs land.

features.name: Political simulation: classes, parties, parliament, laws, unrest and civil war
features.summary: Every nation simulates five social classes (aristocracy, bourgeoisie, ... workers, peasants) with wealth, satisfaction and political activity, four political parties with influence and class support, a government type (monarchy to republic), parliament and executive elections, laws enforced by the ruling party, a budget and corruption, and popular movements (liberal and socialist) that escalate from demonstrations to riots to rebellions; a winning rebellion changes the government and may split the country in civil war. Battle casualties reduce town populations.

features.name: Modified-Native campaign rules (recruitment, autocalc, lords, bandits)
features.summary: Several Native scripts are rewritten to fit the nation simulation: foreign villages no longer give you regular enemy troops - only your own nation's villages do; elsewhere you get regional irregulars/partisans. Auto-resolved battles and captured centres feed the PAS manpower/reinforcement system; lord party size follows the nation's lord count; bandit spawning is regional; volunteers only refresh from the national pool.
features.mechanics: update_volunteer_troops_in_village (44 vs 35 stmts): if the village belongs to the player's kingdom, volunteers are the faction's base troop with random upgrades by relation; otherwise center_get_rebel_troop picks a regional rebel troop (trp_rebel_european1, _balkan1, _turkish1, _indian1, _arab1, _redshirt1 ...) by village culture/position. game_event_simulate_battle (528 vs 396): after a centre falls it calls pas_reinforce_party x3 on the new garrison and pas_faction_end_campaign when a marshal is defeated; recognises pt_pps_rebels. party_get_ideal_size (30 vs 34): from $preferred_ai_party_size and pas_get_faction_ideal_lord_number. create_kingdom_hero_party (22 vs 62): stripped to a plain spawn with generic party name. spawn_bandits (109 vs 178): regional bandit templates (turkish/indian/middleasia/persian/balkan) capped at 150 total. diplomacy_start_war_between_kingdoms (131 vs 86): infamy for wars without casus belli, notifications only for land neighbours. Emptied Native scripts: decide_run_away_or_not, battle_tactic_*, process_player_enterprise, create_village_farmer_party, calculate_castle_prosperities_by_using_its_villages.
